Who I Am

Engineering with precision and purpose.

I am a B.Sc. Mechanical Engineering graduate from the University of Duisburg-Essen (Thesis Grade: 1.0, Overall GPA: 2.0), currently enrolled in M.Sc. Mechanical Engineering from Winter Semester 2026/27.

My practical experience includes a 13-week industrial internship at Cairo West Power Station — a 500 MW combined-cycle plant — where I worked on rotating equipment overhaul, hydraulic performance testing, vibration spectrum analysis, and dimensional inspection to DIN EN ISO standards.

I am driven by the challenge of transforming an engineering problem into a working solution — through CAD design, simulation, or analytical modelling.

Bachelor Thesis · University of Duisburg-Essen · 2026

Analysis of Influences on Roll Force, Torque and Forward Slip in Hot Flat Rolling of Steel by Fast Simulation

Grade: 1.0ROMICALMATLABC55 Steel6 Rolling Theories52 Measured Passes

Six analytical rolling theories were evaluated for their ability to predict roll force, torque, and forward slip in hot flat rolling of C55 steel. The theories were validated against 52 measured passes across five parametric studies covering pass reduction, roll-gap geometry, interstand tensions, friction parameters, and warm strip rolling in a multi-stand configuration.

Study 1 — Effect of Pass Reduction & Roll-Gap Geometry
Alexander theory: rolling force vs. pass reduction.
Sims theory: rolling force prediction.
Study 4 — Comparison to Measured Data
Rolling force: all theories vs. measurements.
Rolling torque: all theories vs. measurements.
Relative prediction error ΔF per theory.
Study 5 — Warm Strip Rolling (Multi-Stand)
Rolling force across stands.
Torque across multiple stands.

Team Project · Team Leader · Mansoura University · 2020

HHO Electrolyzer

SolidWorksAISI 316LElectrochemistryPrototypingTeam of 4

Designed and assembled an HHO (hydrogen-oxygen) electrolyzer as team leader of a 4-person group. Selected AISI 316L stainless steel electrodes for their superior corrosion resistance in alkaline electrolyte environments. Conducted electrochemical efficiency measurements and validated the hydrogen production rate against our design targets. Delivered a functional prototype within one academic semester.

Key Design Decisions

• Electrode material: AISI 316L selected for superior corrosion resistance in alkaline environments
• Electrolyte: KOH solution optimised for conductivity and gas production efficiency
• Cell geometry designed in SolidWorks to maximise electrode surface area
• Safety: flash-back arrestor and pressure relief integrated in the gas circuit

Note: Project files from 2020 are no longer available. Description based on documented project records.

Team Project · Team Leader · Mansoura University · 2019

Dual-Axis Solar Tracking System

SolidWorksArduinoLDR SensorsServo MotorsTeam of 6

Designed and built a dual-axis solar tracking system as team leader of a 6-person group. The system uses 4 LDR sensors to continuously detect the direction of maximum solar irradiance and orient the panel perpendicular to incident sunlight.

System Overview

• Two-axis tracking: azimuth and elevation controlled by two servo motors
• Sensor array: 4 LDR sensors detect irradiance gradient
• Arduino reads differential LDR signals and drives servos
• Aluminium frame designed in SolidWorks for rigidity
• Demonstrated continuous tracking vs. fixed mounting

Note: Project files from 2019 are no longer available.
